claim: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) has an impact on body composition and bone metabolism among its extragonadal effects.
source: Among its extragonadal effects, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) has an impact on body composition and bone metabolism.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as background information, drawing on established scientific understanding.

claim: Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) has a profound impact on circulating FSH concentrations.
source: Since androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) has a profound impact on circulating FSH concentrations, this hormone could potentially be implicated in the changes of fat body mass (FBM), lean body mass (LBM), and bone fragility induced by ADT.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Twenty-nine consecutive non-metastatic prostate cancer patients were enrolled from 2017 to 2019 in a phase IV study.
source: Twenty-nine consecutive non-metastatic prostate cancer (PC) patients were enrolled from 2017 to 2019 in a phase IV study.
evidence: This describes the study design and patient enrollment.

claim: All patients underwent administration of the luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone antagonist degarelix.
source: All patients underwent administration of the luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone antagonist degarelix.
evidence: This describes the treatment intervention in the study.

claim: At baseline conditions, a weak, non-significant, direct relationship was found between FSH serum levels and FBM at arms (r = 0.36) and legs (r = 0.33).
source: At baseline conditions, a weak, non-significant, direct relationship was found between FSH serum levels and FBM at arms (r = 0.36) and legs (r = 0.33).
evidence: This reports correlation coefficients from statistical analysis of baseline data.

claim: A stronger correlation was observed between FSH and total FBM (r = 0.52, p = 0.006) assessed after 12 months.
source: Conversely, a stronger correlation was observed between FSH and total FBM (r = 0.52, p = 0.006), fat mass at arms (r = 0.54, p = 0.004), and fat mass at trunk (r = 0.45, p = 0.018) assessed after 12 months.
evidence: This reports statistically significant correlation coefficients from data collected at 12 months.

claim: A correlation was observed between FSH and fat mass at arms (r = 0.54, p = 0.004) assessed after 12 months.
source: Conversely, a stronger correlation was observed between FSH and total FBM (r = 0.52, p = 0.006), fat mass at arms (r = 0.54, p = 0.004), and fat mass at trunk (r = 0.45, p = 0.018) assessed after 12 months.
evidence: This reports statistically significant correlation coefficients from data collected at 12 months.

claim: A correlation was observed between FSH and fat mass at trunk (r = 0.45, p = 0.018) assessed after 12 months.
source: Conversely, a stronger correlation was observed between FSH and total FBM (r = 0.52, p = 0.006), fat mass at arms (r = 0.54, p = 0.004), and fat mass at trunk (r = 0.45, p = 0.018) assessed after 12 months.
evidence: This reports statistically significant correlation coefficients from data collected at 12 months.

claim: An inverse relationship between serum FSH and appendicular lean mass index/FBM ratio was observed (r = −0.64, p = 0.001).
source: On the other hand, an inverse relationship between serum FSH and appendicular lean mass index/FBM ratio was observed (r = −0.64, p = 0.001).

claim: FSH has been observed to stimulate osteoclastic activity in the animal model.
source: In the animal model, FSH has been observed to stimulate osteoclastic activity and therefore to exert a negative role on bone mass (Sun et al., 2006; Zaidi et al., 2023; Gera et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to preclinical studies.

claim: FSH exerts a negative role on bone mass in animal models.
source: In the animal model, FSH has been observed to stimulate osteoclastic activity and therefore to exert a negative role on bone mass (Sun et al., 2006; Zaidi et al., 2023; Gera et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to preclinical studies and represents an inference from the observed osteoclastic activity.

claim: FSH was found to have a positive action on adipocytes.
source: Furthermore, FSH was found to have a positive action on adipocytes and the blockade of FSH induced by antibodies against FSH receptor caused an increase in bone mass and a reduction of body fat (Liu et al., 2017; Rojekar et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to preclinical studies.

claim: The blockade of FSH induced by antibodies against FSH receptor caused an increase in bone mass and a reduction of body fat.
source: Furthermore, FSH was found to have a positive action on adipocytes and the blockade of FSH induced by antibodies against FSH receptor caused an increase in bone mass and a reduction of body fat (Liu et al., 2017; Rojekar et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to preclinical studies.

claim: Large epidemiologic data have shown significant reductions in bone mineral density (BMD) 2–3 years prior to menopause, when FSH serum levels are increasing.
source: Large epidemiologic data have shown significant reductions in bone mineral density (BMD) and high resorption rates 2–3 years prior to menopause, when FSH serum levels are increasing, which is also associated with increased body weight and visceral adiposity (Thurston et al., 2009; Senapati et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical epidemiologic studies.

claim: High resorption rates occur 2–3 years prior to menopause, when FSH serum levels are increasing.
source: Large epidemiologic data have shown significant reductions in bone mineral density (BMD) and high resorption rates 2–3 years prior to menopause, when FSH serum levels are increasing, which is also associated with increased body weight and visceral adiposity (Thurston et al., 2009; Senapati et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical epidemiologic studies.

claim: Increasing FSH serum levels prior to menopause are associated with increased body weight and visceral adiposity.

claim: A longitudinal study involving post-menopausal women has shown that increases in circulating FSH levels were associated with greater increases in the percentage of total body fat, total body fat mass, and subcutaneous adipose tissue.

claim: FSH levels are correlated with the risk of cardiovascular events.

claim: The impact of FSH on body composition may at least partially explain the observed correlation between FSH levels and the risk of cardiovascular events.

claim: Degarelix administration consistently reduced FSH values.

claim: Higher serum levels of FSH during degarelix treatment were significantly associated with higher total, limbs, and trunk fat mass.
